title: Battery Replacement Warranties — Prorated Adjustment Credit Toward a New Crestline Battery
content:
## Clause

A battery covered by the Battery Replacement Warranties that fails after its free period but within the line's prorated-through months of the purchase date (or the commercial-use figures where the commercial-use terms apply) earns a prorated credit toward a new Crestline battery bought on the same visit. The warranty must be in status active when the adjustment is made.

**Months in service** are the whole calendar months elapsed from the purchase date to the adjustment date; a month is complete on the same day of a later month, falling back to the last day of a shorter month.

**Credit percentage.** The credit percentage is the months remaining in the prorated period (the prorated-through months less the months in service) divided by the prorated-through months, multiplied by 100, with that result rounded down to a whole percent. When it is below the line's smallest percentage issued, nothing is issued. A line whose basis of the credit percentage is "not applicable" has no prorated period.

**Credit amount.** The credit is the credit percentage, taken as a percent, of the replacement price, the current selling price of the same line, with the credit rounded half up to the cent. It is spent only on a same-or-higher line battery on the same visit and has no cash value.

**The new battery and the old warranty.** The new battery is a new sale with its own warranty, its installation charged at the line's installation charge for a battery bought with a prorated credit. The adjusted warranty closes as adjusted on the adjustment date.

## Counting months in service (hypothetical dates)

| Purchase date | Adjustment date | Whole months in service |
|---|---|---|
| 15 January | 14 April | 2 |
| 15 January | 15 April | 3 |
| 31 January | the last day of February | 1 |

## Worked credit (hypothetical figures, not any line's)

Suppose a prorated period of 40 months, a current selling price of the same line of 150.00 and a smallest percentage issued of 5%.

| Months in service | Months remaining | Remaining divided by period, multiplied by 100 | Credit percentage | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 33 | 7 | 17.5 | 17% | 25.50 |
| 38 | 2 | 5 | 5% | 7.50 |
| 39 | 1 | 2.5 | 2%, below 5% | nothing is issued |

On the first row: 7 divided by 40 is 0.175, multiplied by 100 is 17.5, rounded down to 17%; 17% of 150.00 is 25.50.

## Points of judgement

- *What price is the percentage applied to?* The current selling price of the same line on the adjustment date, not the price paid for the failed battery.
- *Can the credit be taken as cash or saved for a later visit?* No; it is spent only on a same-or-higher line battery on the same visit.
- *What happens to the failed battery's warranty?* It closes as adjusted; the new battery carries its own warranty from its own sale.
